What Notebook 4 shows: Large differences are visible at ANC entry, progression to ANC4+, early initiation and ANC8+ attainment. The wealth gradient remains visible even among women who initiated ANC early.
Programme-review focus: Determine whether poorer women face barriers not only to entering ANC but also to sustaining repeated contacts after entry.
Options/issues to examine: Affordability of repeated attendance, indirect costs, transport burden, outreach coverage, service availability and continuity arrangements for economically disadvantaged women.
Guidance anchor: National ANC guidance emphasizes equity, demand, utilization and achievement of the recommended ANC contact schedule.
Local verification needed: Routine ANC data by socioeconomic proxy where available, transport and service-cost information, outreach coverage, qualitative evidence from women and facility-level continuity practices.
Boundary: Wealth is an equity signal. The analysis does not identify which financial or service mechanism causes the observed differences.

What Notebook 4 shows: Longer travel time is associated with lower ANC entry, later initiation and weaker progression toward ANC8+. Differences remain visible among women who initiated ANC early.
Programme-review focus: Identify where geographic access and repeated travel burden may interfere with both ANC entry and continued attendance.
Options/issues to examine: Catchment configuration, outreach arrangements, availability of nearer service points, transport conditions and other context-adapted ANC delivery arrangements.
Guidance anchor: WHO implementation guidance allows ANC delivery approaches to be adapted to context, including facility and community/outreach delivery.
Local verification needed: Facility and catchment maps, travel-time information, outreach coverage, transport availability, service readiness and local attendance patterns.
Boundary: Travel time identifies an access pattern but does not establish which service-delivery model would be effective.

What Notebook 4 shows: Regional differences arise at different ANC pathway stages. Some regions show particularly weak entry, while others show relatively strong entry but weaker later continuation.
Programme-review focus: Diagnose the ANC pathway stage at which each regional gap becomes most visible before selecting a programme response.
Options/issues to examine: Regional and woreda differences in service availability, workforce, facility readiness, outreach, access conditions, scheduling and programme implementation.
Guidance anchor: National and WHO guidance support context-sensitive implementation of ANC while maintaining the same overall standards for timely and continued care.
Local verification needed: Routine ANC indicators by region and woreda, facility readiness, workforce and service-organization data, outreach implementation information and local qualitative evidence.
Boundary: Region is a contextual diagnostic marker, not a causal mechanism or intervention target.

What Notebook 4 shows: ANC8+ attainment is substantially higher among early initiators, and early ANC is the most prominent predictor in the extended models. However, more than half of early initiators still do not reach ANC8+.
Programme-review focus: Separate the problem of timely initiation from the problem of continuity after timely initiation.
Options/issues to examine: Early pregnancy identification and first-contact pathways, followed by appointment scheduling, return-visit systems and continuity of care after the first ANC contact.
Guidance anchor: National and WHO ANC guidance recommend the first contact within the first trimester and a minimum of eight contacts.
Local verification needed: Gestational age at first contact, return-contact patterns, scheduling and appointment systems, missed-return information where available and facility-level continuity practices.
Boundary: The strong observed and model association does not establish a causal effect of early initiation, and its incremental predictive gain remains uncertain.
